ana: Quick heads-up: onboarding run for new-rerank shows ndcg@10 down 2.1% on curated_holdout, mrr@10 up 0.8%. This was after a combined PR that changed snippet clipping (256->200) and enabled url/case normalizer. Anyone seen this pattern?
chris: I saw something similar in a different bring-up. Shorter snippets lose trailing sentences, which can reshuffle mid-tail ranks. Can you paste the exact eval command?
ana: Command I ran: `./ci/eval_rerank --model new-rerank --set curated_holdout --metrics ndcg@10,mrr@10 --seed 7`
zayd: I queued an ablation: snippet=256/224/200, normalizer=off/on, quant=fp16/int8. run id rb-3612.
eval-bot: ablation summary:
```
snippet=256 normalizer=off quant=fp16 -> ndcg@10 0.4287 mrr@10 0.2191
snippet=224 normalizer=off quant=fp16 -> ndcg@10 0.4249 mrr@10 0.2203
snippet=200 normalizer=off quant=fp16 -> ndcg@10 0.4212 mrr@10 0.2210
snippet=256 normalizer=on  quant=fp16 -> ndcg@10 0.4260 mrr@10 0.2200
snippet=224 normalizer=on  quant=fp16 -> ndcg@10 0.4213 mrr@10 0.2215
snippet=200 normalizer=on  quant=fp16 -> ndcg@10 0.4190 mrr@10 0.2227
snippet=200 normalizer=on  quant=int8  -> ndcg@10 0.4168 mrr@10 0.2239
```
chris: Pattern: both shorter snippet and normalizer independently reduce ndcg; combined effect worst. int8 nudges ndcg down further while mrr rises.
zayd: Next steps: 1) try snippet=232 as compromise and run targeted long-doc slice, 2) produce per-query churn CSV for top-10 shifts (I'll do), 3) block canary promotion until holdout_longdoc ndcg within tolerance.
ana: I'll add snippet-length A/B toggle to the canary checklist and open a quick RFC to include snippet/normalizer/quant ablation in onboarding.
eval-bot: hold flag applied for model new-rerank (reason: ndcg regression on holdout_longdoc >1%).
